faq: How often can the flow run?
As often as every few minutes, or on a daily or weekly schedule. Most clients choose daily. We set the schedule with you based on volume and any limits of the tools involved.
What if something stops working after delivery?
The flow sends an alert when a run fails, so you hear about it. Fixes for problems caused by our build are covered in the revision period. Monthly care is quoted separately.
Do I need to keep a computer on?
No. We run the flow in a hosted automation tool in your own account, so it does not depend on your laptop. Hosting or tool subscriptions, if any, are billed to you directly.
Can this include steps from other Data and documents services?
Yes. Reading, extraction, cleaning, checks and spreadsheet delivery can be chained into one flow. Tell us which steps you want and we scope them together.

desc:
Scheduled document processing set-up lets a flow pick up new files on its own, process them and deliver results without anyone pressing a button. Ecom Swift LLC builds it end to end, with a run history, error alerts and a handover guide.

## What is scheduled document processing?

Scheduled document processing means a flow that starts itself. It checks a folder or inbox on a daily or weekly schedule, or when a new file arrives, then reads, extracts and checks each document and sends the results to your sheet or tool. People step in only when an alert or a review list asks them to.

It is the final stage of a data project. Reading and extraction may already work, but if someone must launch them by hand, they still depend on that person remembering.

## Why a flow that needs a person to start it falls behind

Many useful processes die quietly. A weekly import is done diligently for a month, then skipped during a busy week, then forgotten. Results become irregular, reports are based on stale data and nobody is sure which files were processed.

Manual starts also hide errors. If a person runs a job, finds an odd result and moves on, the cause is rarely recorded. A scheduled flow with a history makes each run visible and each failure traceable.

## How hands-off flows change reliability and time

A scheduled flow gives you a steady rhythm. New documents are handled the same way each time, at the time you chose, regardless of who is in the office. Your team stops spending a slot on routine processing and sees only what needs a decision.

The run history shows what was processed, how many items passed checks and what failed. Alerts mean you hear about a problem the same day, not at month-end. The benefit depends on volume and on how stable your documents are, and a flow still needs some care when sources or formats change, which is why handover and optional monthly care are part of the picture.

## What a complete hands-off flow includes

- One or more defined sources, such as a folder, a shared drive or an inbox.
- A schedule or a trigger that matches your pace, such as daily or on arrival.
- Chained steps, for example reading, extraction and accuracy checks in order.
- Results delivered to the sheet, database or tool your team uses.
- A run history that records time, counts and outcomes of each run.
- Alerts by email or chat when a run fails or a threshold is crossed.
- A review list for items that need a person, with an approval step where wanted.
- Retry and error handling, so a temporary fault does not lose files.
- A weekly summary for your team.
- A handover guide and a period of observed runs before we step away.

## How we build and hand it over

We map your current routine on paper first: where files arrive, who touches them, which steps are manual and where the results end up. From the map we agree the flow and what should happen when something goes wrong.

Then we build it in your own accounts, test it with real files and watch several runs. The Basic package covers one source, one processing step, a schedule and one results sheet. Standard chains up to three steps with accuracy checks, a run history, failure alerts and a review list. Premium handles several sources and destinations, approvals for flagged items, a weekly report, retry logic and a test period of runs, then a full handover. Care after that is quoted separately, so you decide whether you want it.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Keep the same folder structure and naming habits that the flow expects.
- Name one person who receives alerts and reads the weekly summary.
- Test any change to a source format before it goes live.
- Keep the handover guide where your whole team can find it.
- Decide how often the flow should run, based on how fast you need results.

**Avoid:**
- Running the flow on a personal laptop that is often switched off.
- Letting alerts go to an inbox nobody reads.
- Renaming or moving the source folder without telling us.
- Adding new document types to the folder before they have been tested.
- Assuming a flow needs no attention at all, forever.

## Who this service is for

It suits an accounting practice that gathers client documents every week and processes them on the same day. It suits a small ecommerce or logistics team that receives supplier files daily. It also suits a business owner who has already seen data processing work and now wants it to continue without staff effort.

## What we need from you

Tell us where files arrive, how often, and where results should go, and share a sample of recent files. Name the person who will receive alerts. We never ask for passwords. Where a platform supports it, you add us as a collaborator, team member or developer user, and everything runs in your own accounts so you keep full control.
